transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start off, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Yeah, um… I guess I’m here because I feel like I’m always running hot, like I can’t shut the motor off. And lately it’s been getting me in trouble at the firehouse.

I mean, that place is already high energy, you know? Alarms, gear, everyone moving—and I usually like that, honestly. It’s kind of why I ended up there. But even when things are supposed to be calm, I’m still… revved up. Like I’m idling too high all the time.
Has this feeling of being constantly 'revved up' been something you've noticed since childhood, or is this a change from how you used to feel?

Yeah, no, it’s not new. I mean, I probably didn’t think of it that way as a kid, but my mom definitely did. She’ll still bring it up—like, “You were always out of your seat,” or I’d blurt out answers before the teacher finished asking, that kind of thing.

And I was bright enough, that’s the annoying part. It wasn’t like I couldn’t do the work. I’d lose the homework or forget to turn it in, and then there’d be notes sent home. My mom kept some of them, actually—she’s one of those people who saves everything in folders, old report cards, baseball pictures, all that. But yeah, going back to grade school, it was already there.

Would you say this 'revved up' feeling has been pretty constant and steady throughout your life, or does it come and go in distinct stretches where you feel noticeably more wired or more down than your usual baseline?

It’s more constant, I’d say. Like, I don’t really have these clear stretches where I’m a totally different person or anything. It’s more like I’m always running hot—like the motor’s always on and I can’t quite shut it off.

And at the firehouse, that’s where it’s been showing up more lately, or maybe people are just more fed up with it. Which is funny because everybody there is kind of amped half the time, but even when we’re supposed to be settled down, I still feel like I’m… buzzing, I guess. It’s just kind of always there.

Outside of work, like at home or when you're trying to relax or focus on something like reading or a conversation, do you notice yourself getting distracted easily or losing track of what you're doing?

Yeah, definitely. I mean, it happens all the time, not just at work. I’ll try to sit down and read something or talk to somebody, and then—like, if the radio chirps, or somebody just walks past the bay, or even some random thought about a call from yesterday pops into my head, I’m gone.

And then I’m sitting there like… wait, what was I doing? It takes me forever to get back to it. Sometimes I’ll start one thing, notice something else, and then I’m halfway into that, and—sorry, what were you asking exactly? Yeah, distracted. Very easily.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others, blurting things out, or making quick decisions/actions without thinking them through, even now as an adult?

Yeah. I mean, that one’s pretty obvious, unfortunately.

At the station, if the guys are talking through a plan, I’ll already have the answer in my head and I just jump in. Like I cut right across somebody before they’re done, and then I can see it on their face—like, okay, I just stepped on them, or threw off the flow of what they were saying.

And it’s not like I’m trying to be a jerk. I just… it feels like if I don’t say it right then, it’s going to disappear or we’re wasting time. Then afterward I’m like, why didn’t I just wait ten seconds?
Have you ever had a period of several days where you felt unusually euphoric or overly self-confident, needed much less sleep than usual, and still felt full of energy the next day?

I don’t think so… not like that, anyway.

I mean, I’ve had days where I feel really keyed up, especially if something big is going on or I’ve got a lot in my head, but several days of feeling, like, amazing and not needing sleep? I’m not sure I’d describe it that way.

Sleep gets weird sometimes with the schedule at the firehouse anyway, so it’s hard to separate what’s “me” from what’s just the job. Like after a busy shift, everybody’s kind of running on fumes and still wired, and then you go home and your brain’s still back at the station. But overly confident or euphoric for days… no, I don’t think I’ve noticed that.

Before this recent trouble at the firehouse, can you think of other times in your life—like in school, previous jobs, or relationships—where this same restlessness, distractibility, or impulsivity actually caused real problems for you?

Yeah… I mean, the biggest thing is what’s happening now at the firehouse. Before that, I don’t know, I could kind of explain stuff away, like everybody forgets something or jumps the gun sometimes.

But now it’s actually costing me trust. I got pulled into this performance and safety meeting, which… honestly, that was embarrassing. And it wasn’t just like “do better,” it was more like the crew needs to know I’m tracking details consistently, and right now they don’t.

And I’ve been wanting to move toward leadership, you know, lieutenant track eventually, and now it feels like that’s slipping. Like people are looking at me like, can we count on him to keep all the pieces straight? And I hate that, because I care about the job. I care a lot. I’m not trying to be careless, it just… it keeps catching up with me.
